root_cause.text: The per-CPU `xdp_dev_bulk_queue` in `kernel/bpf/devmap.c` was protected only by `local_bh_disable()`, which does not prevent preemption on PREEMPT_RT, allowing concurrent `bq_enqueue()` and `__dev_flush()` execution on the same CPU and races on `bq->q[]`, `bq->count`, and `flush_node`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says PREEMPT_RT lets CFS preempt `bq_xmit_all()` because `local_bh_disable()` “only calls migrate_disable() … and does not disable preemption,” so another task can enter `bq_enqueue()` on the same per-CPU `bq`; the patch fixes this by adding `local_lock_t bq_lock` to `struct xdp_dev_bulk_queue` and acquiring it in both `bq_enqueue()` and `__dev_flush()` with `local_lock_nested_bh()`, plus `lockdep_assert_held(&bq->bq_lock)` in `bq_xmit_all()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the local_lock header so the file can use local lock support correctly.
intent_record.what: A new include directive for <linux/local_lock.h> was added immediately after the existing <linux/bpf.h> include.
intent_record.how: This makes the local_lock API and related definitions available to the translation unit, allowing code in this file to use local locks without missing-type or missing-symbol compilation errors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local lock to the XDP bulk queue structure to protect its state from concurrent access.
intent_record.what: A new field, `local_lock_t bq_lock`, was added to `struct xdp_dev_bulk_queue`.
intent_record.how: This introduces a per-bulk-queue local lock that can be used to serialize access to the bulk queue state, helping prevent concurrent races when the queue is manipulated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a lock assertion to ensure bq_xmit_all() is called with bq_lock held.
intent_record.what: A lockdep assertion was added at the start of bq_xmit_all(), calling lockdep_assert_held(&bq->bq_lock) before the existing empty-queue check.
intent_record.how: At runtime in lockdep-enabled builds, this will verify that bq_xmit_all() is only invoked while bq->bq_lock is held, helping catch incorrect lock usage during development and debugging without changing normal execution behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect __dev_flush() with the XDP bulk queue lock to prevent concurrent state corruption during flush processing.
intent_record.what: In __dev_flush(), the code now acquires bq->dev->xdp_bulkq->bq_lock with local_lock_nested_bh() before calling bq_xmit_all(), clearing bq->dev_rx and bq->xdp_prog, and removing bq from the flush list; it then releases the same lock with local_unlock_nested_bh() after the list deletion.
intent_record.how: This serializes the flush path against concurrent accesses to the device bulk queue state, preventing races while transmitting pending XDP bulk packets and while clearing or unlinking the queue entry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Serialize per-CPU XDP bulk queue access with local_lock_nested_bh() to avoid races on PREEMPT_RT.
intent_record.what: In bq_enqueue(), the code was changed from initializing the per-CPU bulk queue pointer directly with this_cpu_ptr(dev->xdp_bulkq) to first declaring bq separately, then acquiring local_lock_nested_bh(&dev->xdp_bulkq->bq_lock) before assigning bq = this_cpu_ptr(dev->xdp_bulkq). A comment was also extended to mention that PREEMPT_RT relies on local_lock_nested_bh() to serialize access to the per-CPU bq.
intent_record.how: This makes access to the per-CPU XDP bulk queue explicitly serialized under PREEMPT_RT, preventing concurrent softirq/RT-thread access from racing on the queue state while preserving the existing enqueue and flush behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix unlock handling in `bq_enqueue()` by releasing the bulk queue lock after enqueueing an XDP frame.
intent_record.what: A call to `local_unlock_nested_bh(&dev->xdp_bulkq->bq_lock);` was added at the end of `bq_enqueue()` after storing the `xdpf` into `bq->q[bq->count++]`.
intent_record.how: This change releases the bulk queue lock after an XDP frame is enqueued, preventing the lock from remaining held past the enqueue operation and allowing subsequent callers or code paths to acquire it correctly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize each per-CPU XDP bulk queue lock during netdevice registration to avoid uninitialized state and ensure safe operation.
intent_record.what: In the NETDEV_REGISTER case of dev_map_notification(), the single-line loop over all possible CPUs was expanded into a block that first assigns each per-CPU xdp_dev_bulk_queue pointer to a local variable, then sets bq->dev = netdev, and additionally initializes bq->bq_lock with local_lock_init().
intent_record.how: At runtime, each per-CPU XDP bulk queue is now fully initialized during device registration, including its local lock, which prevents use of an uninitialized lock state and ensures the queue can be safely used later on.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds the local_lock header; it does not itself fix the PREEMPT_RT race in xdp_dev_bulk_queue or modify the locking around bq_enqueue/__dev_flush to prevent concurrent access.
The change adds a local lock to protect the XDP bulk queue state from concurrent access, which directly addresses the race caused by insufficient protection of `xdp_dev_bulk_queue` on PREEMPT_RT.

The vulnerability is caused by unsafe concurrent access to the per-CPU bulk queue due to insufficient protection. Adding a lock assertion for bq_xmit_all() under bq_lock is directly related to enforcing the needed synchronization around bulk-queue operations, so this change addresses the same root cause area.
The change directly addresses the described race in xdp_dev_bulk_queue by adding locking around __dev_flush(), which is the same concurrency issue caused by insufficient protection on PREEMPT_RT.

The change directly matches the root cause: it replaces insufficient BH-only protection for the per-CPU XDP bulk queue with local_lock_nested_bh() to serialize access and prevent PREEMPT_RT races on bq->q[], bq->count, and flush_node.

The root cause is an insufficient protection of the per-CPU bulk queue on PREEMPT_RT, leading to preemption races between bq_enqueue() and __dev_flush(). This group only fixes lock/unlock handling in bq_enqueue() and does not address the preemption/concurrency protection issue described.

The root cause is a PREEMPT_RT race from using only local_bh_disable() to protect the per-CPU xdp_dev_bulk_queue, requiring stronger synchronization. This group only initializes the bulk queue lock during netdevice registration and addresses uninitialized state, not the concurrency race on bq->q[], bq->count, or flush_node.

candidates.rationale: This flush path iterates and mutates the shared per-CPU bulk queue state without taking any lock, so on PREEMPT_RT it can race with concurrent enqueue activity on the same CPU.
This statement operates on the bulk queue during flush while the queue is only protected by local_bh_disable(), allowing concurrent bq_enqueue() to corrupt bq->q[] or bq->count.
This unsynchronized state reset is part of the flush race: another concurrent enqueue on the same CPU can observe or overwrite the bulk queue fields while flush is modifying them.
This clears shared bulk-queue metadata without locking, which is vulnerable to concurrent access from bq_enqueue() and can lead to inconsistent queue state.
This enqueue-side check/read of bq->count is performed on the per-CPU queue without a real lock, so PREEMPT_RT preemption can race with __dev_flush() and corrupt the queue accounting.

vuln_statements.explanation: This enqueue-side read of the shared per-CPU bulk queue counter occurs without proper exclusion on PREEMPT_RT. Since local_bh_disable() does not prevent preemption there, it can race with __dev_flush() on the same CPU and contribute to corruption of bq->count and related queue state.

The flush path iterates over the shared per-CPU bulk queue list without taking the XDP bulk queue lock, so it can run concurrently with bq_enqueue() on PREEMPT_RT and race on flush_node and other bulk queue state.

This flush-time operation acts on the shared bulk queue state without real locking, allowing concurrent enqueue activity to interfere with bq->q[] and bq->count while __dev_flush() is processing the queue.
This unsynchronized reset of shared per-CPU queue metadata is part of the flush race and can be concurrently observed or overwritten by bq_enqueue() on the same CPU.
This clears shared bulk-queue metadata without proper locking, so concurrent enqueue/flush activity on PREEMPT_RT can race and leave the queue in an inconsistent state.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code no longer matches the vulnerable construct described in the root cause. The race was around the per-CPU bulk queue being accessed under only local_bh_disable() while both enqueue and flush manipulated shared fields like `bq->q[]`, `bq->count`, and `flush_node`. In this snippet, the devmap XDP program is moved out of enqueue and into flush: `bq_enqueue()` only stores `dev_rx`, `xdp_prog`, and adds the queue to the flush list once (`if (!bq->dev_rx) { ... list_add(&bq->flush_node, flush_list); }`), while `__dev_flush()` performs `bq_xmit_all(bq, XDP_XMIT_FLUSH);` and then clears `bq->dev_rx`, `bq->xdp_prog`, and removes the node. The prior per-packet program execution function `dev_map_run_prog()` is deleted, and `dev_map_enqueue()` now just calls `__xdp_enqueue(..., dst->xdp_prog)`. So the vulnerable concurrent `bq_enqueue()`/`__dev_flush()` interaction on `xdp_prog` handling is not present here; this commit changes the logic in a way that avoids that specific construct rather than exhibiting it.

Author: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <hawk@kernel.org>

    bpf: Run devmap xdp_prog on flush instead of bulk enqueue
    
    This changes the devmap XDP program support to run the program when the
    bulk queue is flushed instead of before the frame is enqueued. This has
    a couple of benefits:

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown diff moves devmap XDP program execution out of bulk enqueue and into flush-time processing, which matches the fix for the stated race. In particular, the old per-packet path `dev_map_run_prog()` is removed, and `dev_map_enqueue()` now just calls `__xdp_enqueue(dev, xdp, dev_rx, dst->xdp_prog)` without running the program immediately. The program is stored in the per-CPU bulk queue (`struct xdp_dev_bulk_queue { ... struct bpf_prog *xdp_prog; ... }`), set together with `dev_rx` in `bq_enqueue()` (`if (!bq->dev_rx) { bq->dev_rx = dev_rx; bq->xdp_prog = xdp_prog; list_add(&bq->flush_node, flush_list); }`), and then consumed in `bq_xmit_all()` via `dev_map_bpf_prog_run(bq->xdp_prog, bq->q, cnt, dev)`. The comment in `__dev_flush()` explicitly notes the paired update/clear: `bq->dev_rx = NULL; bq->xdp_prog = NULL; __list_del_clearprev(&bq->flush_node);`. Since the vulnerability root cause was concurrent access during bulk enqueue versus flush under PREEMPT_RT, this commit already contains the corrective restructuring and therefore does not show the vulnerable construct as present in its vulnerable form.
